data.name: Aabid
data.gender_notes: Aabid is used as a male name in Arabic and Muslim naming tradition.
data.long_meaning: Aabid (عابد) is an Arabic name meaning “Worshipper; devout servant (of God)”. It comes from Arabic ʿābid (عابد) 'worshipper, devout servant', the active participle of ʿabada 'to worship'. The active participle ʿābid denotes one who is actively engaged in ʿibādah (worship). It is distinct from Aabad (آباد, Persian 'inhabited'), despite the similar English spelling.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aabid carries the meaning Worshipper; devout servant of God. The name expresses religious devotion; this is its documented lexical sense rather than an added doctrinal claim.
data.etymology: From Arabic ʿābid (عابد) 'worshipper, devout servant', active participle of ʿabada 'to worship'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabid total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What does the name Aabid mean?
faq.a: Aabid means Worshipper; devout servant (of God).

faq.q: What is the origin of the name Aabid?
What language does the name Aabid come from?
faq.a: Aabid is used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian and Pashto.

faq.q: Is Aabid a boy's name or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aabid is used as a male name.

faq.q: How is Aabid written in Arabic?
faq.a: Aabid is written عابد in Arabic, Urdu and Pashto, and आबिद in Devanagari.

faq.q: What is the linguistic root of Aabid?
faq.a: The root of Aabid is ʿ-b-d (ع-ب-د), from ʿābid (عابد).

faq.q: What is the etymology of Aabid?
faq.a: From Arabic ʿābid (عابد) worshipper, devout servant, the active participle of ʿabada, to worship.

faq.q: Does Aabid appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aabid is not itself a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: What is the feminine form of Aabid?
faq.a: The feminine form is ʿĀbidah (عابدة), meaning a female worshipper, listed in this dataset as Aabida.

faq.q: Is Aabid related to the name Abd?
faq.a: Yes. Both come from the root ʿ-b-d, to serve and to worship. Abd appears in theophoric names such as ʿAbdullāh, servant of God.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aabid verified?
faq.a: Yes. The meaning Worshipper rests on the Arabic active participle ʿābid, from the root ʿ-b-d.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Aabid?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aabid total 18, reducing to 9. Number 9 is traditionally associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Aabid?
faq.a: Variants and alternative transliterations include Abid and Aabed.

faq.q: Is Aabid the same as Aabad?
faq.a: No. Aabid (عابد) means worshipper and comes from Arabic. Aabad (آباد) means inhabited and comes from Persian. They are unrelated despite the similar English spelling.
